agent.system_template:
You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# Workflow to build your docs with oranda (and mdbook)
# and deploy them to Github Pages
name: Web

# We're going to push to the gh-pages branch, so we need that permission
permissions:
  contents: write

# What situations do we want to build docs in?
# All of these work independently and can be removed / commented out
# if you don't want oranda/mdbook running in that situation
on:
  # Check that a PR didn't break docs!
  #
  # Note that the "Deploy to Github Pages" step won't run in this mode,
  # so this won't have any side-effects. But it will tell you if a PR
  # completely broke oranda/mdbook. Sadly we don't provide previews (yet)!
  pull_request:

  # Whenever something gets pushed to main, update the docs!
  # This is great for getting docs changes live without cutting a full release.
  #
  # Note that if you're using cargo-dist, this will "race" the Release workflow
  # that actually builds the Github Release that oranda tries to read (and
  # this will almost certainly complete first). As a result you will publish
  # docs for the latest commit but the oranda landing page won't know about
  # the latest release. The workflow_run trigger below will properly wait for
  # cargo-dist, and so this half-published state will only last for ~10 minutes.
  #
  # If you only want docs to update with releases, disable this, or change it to
  # a "release" branch. You can, of course, also manually trigger a workflow run
  # when you want the docs to update.
  push:
    branches:
      - main

  # Whenever a workflow called "Release" completes, update the docs!
  #
  # If you're using cargo-dist, this is recommended, as it will ensure that
  # oranda always sees the latest release right when it's available. Note
  # however that Github's UI is wonky when you use workflow_run, and won't
  # show this workflow as part of any commit. You have to go to the "actions"
  # tab for your repo to see this one running (the gh-pages deploy will also
  # only show up there).
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [ "Release" ]
    types:
      - completed

# Alright, let's do it!
jobs:
  web:
    name: Build and deploy site and docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # Setup
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      # If you use any mdbook plugins, here's the place to install them!

      # Install and run oranda (and mdbook)!
      #
      # This will write all output to ./public/ (including copying mdbook's output to there).
      - name: Install and run oranda
        run: |
          curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/axodotdev/oranda/releases/download/v0.6.1/oranda-installer.sh | sh
          oranda build
      
      - name: Prepare HTML for link checking
        # untitaker/hyperlink supports no site prefixes, move entire site into
        # a subfolder
        run: mkdir /tmp/public/ && cp -R public /tmp/public/oranda

      - name: Check HTML for broken internal links
        uses: untitaker/hyperlink@0.1.29
        with:
          args: /tmp/public/
      
      # Deploy to our gh-pages branch (creating it if it doesn't exist).
      # The "public" dir that oranda made above will become the root dir
      # of this branch.
      #
      # Note that once the gh-pages branch exists, you must
      # go into repo's settings > pages and set "deploy from branch: gh-pages".
      # The other defaults work fine.
      - name: Deploy to Github Pages
        uses: JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.4.1
        # ONLY if we're on main (so no PRs or feature branches allowed!)
        if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
        with:
          branch: gh-pages
          # Gotta tell the action where to find oranda's output
          folder: public
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          single-commit: true</output>

---/tmp/gci1/.github/workflows/web.yml
# Workflow to build your docs with oranda (and mdbook)
# and deploy them to Github Pages
name: Web

# We're going to push to the gh-pages branch, so we need that permission
permissions:
  contents: write

# What situations do we want to build docs in?
# All of these work independently and can be removed / commented out
# if you don't want oranda/mdbook running in that situation
on:
  # Check that a PR didn't break docs!
  #
  # Note that the "Deploy to Github Pages" step won't run in this mode,
  # so this won't have any side-effects. But it will tell you if a PR
  # completely broke oranda/mdbook. Sadly we don't provide previews (yet)!
  pull_request:

  # Whenever something gets pushed to main, update the docs!
  # This is great for getting docs changes live without cutting a full release.
  #
  # Note that if you're using cargo-dist, this will "race" the Release workflow
  # that actually builds the Github Release that oranda tries to read (and
  # this will almost certainly complete first). As a result you will publish
  # docs for the latest commit but the oranda landing page won't know about
  # the latest release. The workflow_run trigger below will properly wait for
  # cargo-dist, and so this half-published state will only last for ~10 minutes.
  #
  # If you only want docs to update with releases, disable this, or change it to
  # a "release" branch. You can, of course, also manually trigger a workflow run
  # when you want the docs to update.
  push:
    branches:
      - main

  # Whenever a workflow called "Release" completes, update the docs!
  #
  # If you're using cargo-dist, this is recommended, as it will ensure that
  # oranda always sees the latest release right when it's available. Note
  # however that Github's UI is wonky when you use workflow_run, and won't
  # show this workflow as part of any commit. You have to go to the "actions"
  # tab for your repo to see this one running (the gh-pages deploy will also
  # only show up there).
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [ "Release" ]
    types:
      - completed

# Alright, let's do it!
jobs:
  web:
    name: Build and deploy site and docs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # Setup
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2

      # If you use any mdbook plugins, here's the place to install them!

      # Install and run oranda (and mdbook)!
      #
      # This will write all output to ./public/ (including copying mdbook's output to there).
      - name: Install and run oranda
        run: |
          curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -LsSf https://github.com/axodotdev/oranda/releases/download/v0.6.1/oranda-installer.sh | sh
          oranda build
      
      - name: Prepare HTML for link checking
        # untitaker/hyperlink supports no site prefixes, move entire site into
        # a subfolder
        run: mkdir /tmp/public/ && cp -R public /tmp/public/oranda

      - name: Check HTML for broken internal links
        uses: untitaker/hyperlink@0.1.29
        with:
          args: /tmp/public/
      
      # Deploy to our gh-pages branch (creating it if it doesn't exist).
      # The "public" dir that oranda made above will become the root dir
      # of this branch.
      #
      # Note that once the gh-pages branch exists, you must
      # go into repo's settings > pages and set "deploy from branch: gh-pages".
      # The other defaults work fine.
      - name: Deploy to Github Pages
        uses: JamesIves/github-pages-deploy-action@v4.4.1
        # ONLY if we're on main (so no PRs or feature branches allowed!)
        if: ${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
        with:
          branch: gh-pages
          # Gotta tell the action where to find oranda's output
          folder: public
          token: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          single-commit: true</output>

/* Code modified from the blender website
 * https://www.blender.org/wp-content/themes/bthree/assets/js/get_os.js?x82196
 */

let options = {
    windows64: "x86_64-pc-windows",
    windows32: "i686-pc-windows",
    windowsArm: "aarch64-pc-windows",

    mac64: "x86_64-apple",
    mac32: "i686-apple",
    macSilicon: "aarch64-apple",

    linux64: "x86_64-unknown-linux",
    linux32: "i686-unknown-linux",
    linuxArm: "aarch64-unknown-linux",

    // ios: "ios",
    // android: "linux-android",
    // freebsd: "freebsd",
};

function isAppleSilicon() {
    try {
        var glcontext = document.createElement("canvas").getContext("webgl");
        var debugrenderer = glcontext
            ? glcontext.getExtension("WEBGL_debug_renderer_info")
            : null;
        var renderername =
            (debugrenderer &&
                glcontext.getParameter(debugrenderer.UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL)) ||
            "";
        if (renderername.match(/Apple M/) || renderername.match(/Apple GPU/)) {
            return true;
        }

        return false;
    } catch (e) {}
}

function getOS() {
    var OS = options.windows64.default;
    var userAgent = navigator.userAgent;
    var platform = navigator.platform;

    if (navigator.appVersion.includes("Win")) {
        if (
            !userAgent.includes("Windows NT 5.0") &&
            !userAgent.includes("Windows NT 5.1") &&
            (userAgent.indexOf("Win64") > -1 ||
                platform == "Win64" ||
                userAgent.indexOf("x86_64") > -1 ||
                userAgent.indexOf("x86_64") > -1 ||
                userAgent.indexOf("amd64") > -1 ||
                userAgent.indexOf("AMD64") > -1 ||
                userAgent.indexOf("WOW64") > -1)
        ) {
            OS = options.windows64;
        } else {
            if (
                window.external &&
                window.external.getHostEnvironmentValue &&
                window.external
                    .getHostEnvironmentValue("os-architecture")
                    .includes("ARM64")
            ) {
                OS = options.windowsArm;
            } else {
                try {
                    var canvas = document.createElement("canvas");
                    var gl = canvas.getContext("webgl");

                    var debugInfo = gl.getExtension("WEBGL_debug_renderer_info");
                    var renderer = gl.getParameter(debugInfo.UNMASKED_RENDERER_WEBGL);
                    if (renderer.includes("Qualcomm")) OS = options.windowsArm;
                } catch (e) {}
            }
        }
    }

    //MacOS, MacOS X, macOS
    if (navigator.appVersion.includes("Mac")) {
        if (
            navigator.userAgent.includes("OS X 10.5") ||
            navigator.userAgent.includes("OS X 10.6")
        ) {
            OS = options.mac32;
        } else {
            OS = options.mac64;

            const isSilicon = isAppleSilicon();
            if (isSilicon) {
                OS = options.macSilicon;
            }
        }
    }

    // linux
    if (platform.includes("Linux")) {
        OS = options.linux64;
        // FIXME: Can we find out whether linux 32-bit or ARM are used?
    }

    // if (
    //     userAgent.includes("iPad") ||
    //     userAgent.includes("iPhone") ||
    //     userAgent.includes("iPod")
    // ) {
    //     OS = options.ios;
    // }
    // if (platform.toLocaleLowerCase().includes("freebsd")) {
    //     OS = options.freebsd;
    // }

    return OS;
}

let os = getOS();
window.os = os;

// Unhide and hydrate selector with events
const archSelect = document.querySelector(".arch-select");
if (archSelect) {
    archSelect.classList.remove("hidden");
    const selector = document.querySelector("#install-arch-select");
    if (selector) {
        selector.addEventListener("change", onArchChange);
    }
}

// Hydrate tab buttons with events
Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(".install-tab[data-id]")).forEach((tab) => {
    tab.addEventListener("click", onTabClick);
});

function onArchChange(evt) {
    // Get target
    const target = evt.currentTarget.value;
    // Find corresponding installer lists
    const newContentEl = document.querySelector(`.arch[data-arch=${target}]`);
    const oldContentEl = document.querySelector(`.arch[data-arch]:not(.hidden)`);
    // Hide old content element (if applicable)
    if (oldContentEl) {
        oldContentEl.classList.add("hidden");
    }
    // Show new content element
    newContentEl.classList.remove("hidden");
    // Show the first tab's content if nothing was selected before
    if (newContentEl.querySelectorAll(".install-tab.selected").length === 0) {
        const firstContentChild = newContentEl.querySelector(".install-content:first-of-type");
        const firstTabChild = newContentEl.querySelector(".install-tab:first-of-type");
        firstContentChild.classList.remove("hidden");
        if (firstTabChild) {
            firstTabChild.classList.add("selected");
        }
    }
    // Hide "no OS detected" message
    const noDetectEl = document.querySelector(".no-autodetect");
    noDetectEl.classList.add("hidden");
    // Hide Mac hint
    document.querySelector(".mac-switch").classList.add("hidden");
}

function onTabClick(evt) {
    // Get target and ID
    const {triple, id} = evt.currentTarget.dataset;
    if (triple) {
        // Find corresponding content elements
        const newContentEl = document.querySelector(`.install-content[data-id="${String(id)}"][data-triple=${triple}]`);
        const oldContentEl = document.querySelector(`.install-content[data-triple=${triple}][data-id]:not(.hidden)`);
        // Find old tab to unselect
        const oldTabEl = document.querySelector(`.install-tab[data-triple=${triple}].selected`);
        // Hide old content element
        if (oldContentEl && oldTabEl) {
            oldContentEl.classList.add("hidden");
            oldTabEl.classList.remove("selected");
        }

        // Unhide new content element
        newContentEl.classList.remove("hidden");
        // Select new tab element
        evt.currentTarget.classList.add("selected");
    }
}

const allPlatforms = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(`.arch[data-arch]`));
let hit = allPlatforms.find(
    (a) => {
        // Show Intel Mac downloads if no M1 Mac downloads are available
        if (
            a.attributes["data-arch"].value.includes(options.mac64) &&
            os.includes(options.macSilicon) &&
            !allPlatforms.find(p => p.attributes["data-arch"].value.includes(options.macSilicon))) {
            // Unhide hint
            document.querySelector(".mac-switch").classList.remove("hidden");
            return true;
        }
        return a.attributes["data-arch"].value.includes(os);
    }
);

if (hit) {
    hit.classList.remove("hidden");
    const selectEl = document.querySelector("#install-arch-select");
    selectEl.value = hit.dataset.arch;
    const firstContentChild = hit.querySelector(".install-content:first-of-type");
    const firstTabChild = hit.querySelector(".install-tab:first-of-type");
    firstContentChild.classList.remove("hidden");
    if (firstTabChild) {
        firstTabChild.classList.add("selected");
    }
} else {
    const noDetectEl = document.querySelector(".no-autodetect");
    if (noDetectEl) {
        const noDetectElDetails = document.querySelector(".no-autodetect-details");
        if (noDetectElDetails) {
            noDetectElDetails.innerHTML = `We detected you're on ${os} but there don't seem to be installers for that. `
        }
        noDetectEl.classList.remove("hidden");
    }
}

let copyButtons = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll("[data-copy]"));
if (copyButtons.length) {
    copyButtons.forEach(function (element) {
        element.addEventListener("click", () => {
            navigator.clipboard.writeText(element.attributes["data-copy"].value);
        });
    });
}

// Toggle for pre releases
const checkbox = document.getElementById("show-prereleases");

if (checkbox) {
    checkbox.addEventListener("click", () => {
        const all = document.getElementsByClassName("pre-release");

        if (all) {
            for (var item of all) {
                item.classList.toggle("hidden");
            }
        }
    });

import os, subprocess, sys, shutil, json, pathlib
def run(name, files):
    base=f"/tmp/cases/{name}"
    shutil.rmtree(base, ignore_errors=True); os.makedirs(base, exist_ok=True)
    for k,v in files.items():
        p=os.path.join(base,k); os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(p), exist_ok=True) if os.path.dirname(k) else None
        with open(p,'w') as f: f.write(v)
    env=os.environ.copy(); env["ORANDA_CSS"]="/tmp/cssdir/oranda.css"
    r=subprocess.run(["/workspace/executable","build"], cwd=base, env=env, capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=10)
    out={"exit":r.returncode,"stdout":r.stdout,"stderr":r.stderr,"files":{}}

            rel=os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root,fn),base)

            except Exception as e: out["files"][rel]=str(e)
    with open(f"/tmp/cases/{name}.json","w") as f: json.dump(out,f,indent=2)
    print(name, r.returncode, list(out["files"].keys()))
    if r.stdout: print(" OUT",r.stdout.replace("\n"," | ")[:500])

def jaro(s1,s2):
    if s1==s2: return 1.0
    len1,len2=len(s1),len(s2)
    if not len1 or not len2: return 0.0
    md=max(max(len1,len2)//2-1,0)

                # embedded newlines in a cause: first line wrapped, rest verbatim-ish
                if "\n" in str(cause):
                    parts = str(cause).split("\n")
                    lines.extend(_wrap_simple(parts[0], first_p, cont_p))
                    for extra in parts[1:]:
                        lines.append(cont_p + extra if extra else cont_p.rstrip())
                else:
                    lines.extend(_wrap_simple(cause, first_p, cont_p))
        if self.help_text is not None:
            lines.extend(_wrap_simple(self.help_text, "  help: ", "        "))
        return "\n".join(lines) + "\n\n"

    def _snippet(self):
        text = self.source_text
        offset = self.label_offset or 0
        # line/col of offset (byte offset in original; our offsets are char offsets in decoded text matching for ascii)
        # compute line index
        before = text[:offset]
        line_no = before.count("\n") + 1  # 1-based line containing label
        lines_text = text.split("\n")
        # If offset points past end (EOF), line_no may be len+1
        start_line = max(1, line_no-1) if line_no>1 else 1
        # miette header: [file:start_line:1] where start_line is first shown line?
        # Observed: error line 3 -> header :2:1, error line1 -> :1:1
        header_line = start_line
        out = []
        out.append(f"   \u256d\u2500[{self.filename}:{header_line}:1]")
        # show from start_line to min(line_no+1, len)
        # width of line numbers
        end_line = min(len(lines_text), line_no+1) if line_no <= len(lines_text) else len(lines_text)
        if line_no > len(lines_text):
            end_line = len(lines_text)
        # column within error line
        # offset may be on the error line; if offset at EOF after last char, column ?
        for ln in range(start_line, end_line+1):
            content = lines_text[ln-1] if ln-1 < len(lines_text) else ""
            out.append(f" {ln} \u2502 {content}" if content else f" {ln} \u2502")
            if ln == line_no or (line_no > len(lines_text) and ln == end_line):
                # column: offset - start of that line
                line_start = 0
                for k in range(ln-1):
                    line_start += len(lines_text[k]) + 1
                col = offset - line_start  # 0-based
                if col < 0: col = 0
                out.append("   \u00b7 " + " "*col + "\u2500")
        out.append("   \u2570\u2500\u2500\u2500\u2500")
        return out

    def __init__(self, location, panic_message):
        super().__init__("oranda panicked.", causes=[f"at {location}", panic_message], help_text="set the `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace.")
        self.location = location
        self.panic_message = panic_message

def emit_error(err):
    """Fatal error path: json diagnostic to stdout if requested, graphical to stderr, exit 255."""
    if OUTPUT_FORMAT == "json":
        _stdout_write(json.dumps(err.json_obj(), separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
    _stderr_write(err.render())
    raise SystemExit(255)

def emit_warning_diag(err):
    """Non-fatal diagnostic printed graphically to stderr."""
    # In json mode, non-fatal diagnostics are still graphical only (observed)
    _stderr_write(err.render())

def emit_simple_warning(message):
    _stderr_write(f"  \u26a0 {message}\n\n")

def os_error_str(e):
    # Python OSError -> Rust style "msg (os error N)"
    err_no = e.errno if isinstance(e, OSError) else None
    if err_no is not None:
        msg = os.strerror(err_no)
        # Python strerror already is Rust-like text
        return f"{msg} (os error {err_no})"
    return str(e)

# ------------------------------------------------------------ build implementation

def _clean_dist(dist_dir):
    # original appears to remove the dist dir contents before building
    # Avoid catastrophic deletes for "." or "/"
    if dist_dir in (".", "./", "/"):
        # mkdir and remove files? We'll just make sure it exists and remove known outputs later
        os.makedirs(dist_dir, exist_ok=True)
        return
    if os.path.isdir(dist_dir):
        try:
            shutil.rmtree(dist_dir)
        except OSError:
            pass
    os.makedirs(dist_dir, exist_ok=True)

def _write_text_file(path, text):
    # raises Oranda write error style if fails?
    parent=os.path.dirname(path)
    if parent:
        os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
        f.write(text)

def _write_bytes_file(path, data):
    parent=os.path.dirname(path)
    if parent:
        os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
    with open(path, "wb") as f:
        f.write(data)

def copy_static(ctx):
    src=ctx.static_dir
    if not src:
        return
    if not os.path.exists(src):
        return
    # copy into dist/<basename(src)>
    base=os.path.basename(os.path.normpath(src)) if os.path.normpath(src) not in (".",) else ""
    # static file case
    if os.path.isfile(src):
        dest=os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, os.path.basename(src))
        try:
            shutil.copyfile(src, dest)
        except OSError:
            pass
        return
    dest_root=os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, base) if base else ctx.dist_dir
    for root, dirs, files in os.walk(src):
        rel=os.path.relpath(root, src)
        for fn in files:
            sp=os.path.join(root,fn)
            dp=os.path.join(dest_root, rel, fn) if rel!="." else os.path.join(dest_root, fn)
            try:
                os.makedirs(os.path.dirname(dp), exist_ok=True)
                shutil.copyfile(sp, dp)
            except OSError:
                pass

def resolve_mdbook_path(ctx):
    layer=ctx.mdbook_layer or {}
    if layer.get("path"):
        return layer.get("path")
    for cand in [".", "book", "docs"]:
        if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(cand,"book.toml")):
            return cand
    return None

    ctx = build_context(config_path_arg, json_only=json_only)
    ctx._logo_url_for_page = None
    ctx._logo_bytes = None
    ctx._logo_filename = None
    # nav defaults (set later)
    ctx._nav_additional = []
    ctx._nav_artifacts = False
    ctx._nav_mdbook = False
    ctx._nav_funding = False
    ctx._nav_changelog = False
    # obtain releases (may raise fatal repo parse)
    # For json_only, releases are still fetched (as observed)
    obtain_releases(ctx)
    # artifacts warning if needed
    artifacts_warning_needed = False
    # In json-only mode, the whole site build is skipped except artifacts json and installer files
    if json_only:
        # dist clean? Observed json-only creates dist dir but does not clean? It created public with only artifacts.json; stale files? Test later. It does not remove existing? We'll follow observed: create dist, do not clean? But original json-only in fresh dir made public empty except artifacts.
        # Determine artifacts generation
        os.makedirs(ctx.dist_dir, exist_ok=True)
        # If artifacts enabled and repository present (or ...?) artifacts.json is written
        # From cases: artifacts_pm with repo -> artifacts.json; without repo? json-only for artifacts_pm_norepo gave no artifacts.json? Let's check: earlier build --json-only on artifacts cases? We only tested full. Model: if artifacts_enabled:
        if ctx.artifacts_enabled:
            # Warning about no releases is emitted regardless repo? In artifacts_pm json-only, warning emitted. It used repo presence? We'll emit if no releases detected.
            if not ctx.releases or not ctx.releases.releases:
                warn_user("You seem to have release automation set up, but we didn't detect any releases. The install page and associated widget will be empty. To disable this, set `artifacts: false`")
            model,_ = artifacts_model(ctx)
            # When does artifacts.json get written? If repository is None, original json-only for pm_norepo ??? Assume only if... We will write if artifacts_enabled (check tests later)
            try:
                _write_text_file(os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, "artifacts.json"), json.dumps(model, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=False))
            except OSError as e:
                raise OrandaError(f"failed to write a new asset to {os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir,'artifacts.json')}.", causes=[os_error_str(e)], help_text="Make sure you have the correct permissions to create a new file.")
        else:
            # no artifacts: still warning? If cargo_dist etc no.
            pass
        success(f"Your site build is located in `{ctx.dist_dir}`.")
        return ctx
    # full build
    # Clean dist and write initial assets
    _clean_dist(ctx.dist_dir)
    # CSS
    css_bytes=None; css_filename="oranda.css"
    if "ORANDA_CSS" in os.environ:
        override=os.environ["ORANDA_CSS"]
        warn_user(f"Overriding oranda_css path with {override}")
        # read local asset (always local)
        css_bytes = load_local_asset_bytes(override)
        css_filename = os.path.basename(override.rstrip("/")) if override else ""
        # If basename empty, read would have failed for directory etc; keep
        if not css_filename:
            # asset filename determination error (like config-schema empty output)
            raise OrandaError(f"could not determine file name for asset at {override}", help_text="Make sure your path is relative to your oranda config or project manifest file.")
    else:
        # fetch oranda.css
        version=ctx.oranda_css_version
        proxy_url=f"https://octolotl.axodotdev.host/downloads/axodotdev/oranda/{version}/oranda.css"
        direct_url=f"https://api.github.com/repos/axodotdev/oranda/releases/download/{version}/oranda.css"
        try:
            css_bytes = fetch_with_proxy(proxy_url, direct_url)
        except FetchFailure as e:
            # fatal CSS error: message is first cause, causes are rest
            raise OrandaError(e.causes[0], causes=e.causes[1:])
        css_filename="oranda.css"
    # default favicon before CSS? Observed favicon present even when CSS fetching fails.
    # Our order: if CSS fails above, favicon would not be written. To match, write default favicon before CSS fetch when not using override? Reorder logic handled by pre-writing:
    # (We already fetched, so for failure case we need to mimic. This function will be restructured by caller? Instead we handle by writing favicon before fetch in code path above by moving logic - see note)
    # Write CSS
    if css_bytes is not None:
        _write_bytes_file(os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, css_filename), css_bytes if isinstance(css_bytes,(bytes,bytearray)) else str(css_bytes).encode())
    # favicon default
    if not ctx.favicon_path:
        favicon_bytes=base64.b64decode(FAVICON_B64) if FAVICON_B64 else b""
        _write_bytes_file(os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, "favicon.ico"), favicon_bytes)
    # --- pre-component preparation
    # logo loading
    if ctx.logo_path:
        logo_bytes = load_remote_or_local_asset(ctx.logo_path, duplicate_cause=True)
        ctx._logo_bytes = logo_bytes
        if ctx.logo_path.startswith("http://") or ctx.logo_path.startswith("https://"):
            logo_name=os.path.basename(urllib.parse.urlparse(ctx.logo_path).path)
        else:
            logo_name=os.path.basename(ctx.logo_path)
        ctx._logo_filename = logo_name
        ctx._logo_url_for_page = site_url(ctx, logo_name)
    # additional pages processing
    additional_pages_data=[]  # list of (label, source_path, slug_path, md_html, output_rel_path)
    if ctx.additional_pages:
        for label, source_path in ctx.additional_pages.items():
            # extension check
            # path extension lower
            ext=os.path.splitext(source_path)[1].lower()
            if ext != ".md":
                warn_user(f"File {source_path} in additional pages is not markdown and will be skipped")
                continue
            if not os.path.exists(source_path):
                raise OrandaError(f"Specified path `{source_path}` was not found on your filesystem!", help_text="Make sure you specify your path relative to the oranda.json/manifest file/README file of your project!")
            # read asset
            content_bytes=load_local_asset_bytes(source_path)
            try:
                content_text=content_bytes.decode("utf-8")
            except UnicodeDecodeError:
                content_text=content_bytes.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            md_html=render_markdown(content_text, ctx)
            slug_path=source_path[:-len(os.path.splitext(source_path)[1])] if os.path.splitext(source_path)[1] else source_path
            # output file is dist/<source_path> (as observed)
            additional_pages_data.append((label, source_path, slug_path, md_html))
    ctx._additional_pages_data=additional_pages_data
    # nav flags
    ctx._nav_additional=[(label, site_url(ctx, slug_path+"/")) for (label, source_path, slug_path, md_html) in additional_pages_data]
    ctx._nav_artifacts=ctx.artifacts_enabled
    ctx._nav_mdbook=ctx.mdbook_enabled
    ctx._nav_funding=ctx.funding_enabled
    ctx._nav_changelog=bool(ctx.changelog_enabled and ctx.repository)
    # mdbook early path resolution error
    ctx._mdbook_resolved_path=None
    if ctx.mdbook_enabled:
        layer=ctx.mdbook_layer or {}
        if not layer.get("path"):
            resolved=resolve_mdbook_path(ctx)
            if resolved is None:
                raise OrandaError("Couldn't find your book.toml", help_text="You can manually specify path in your components.mdbook config")
            ctx._mdbook_resolved_path=resolved
        else:
            ctx._mdbook_resolved_path=layer.get("path")
    # INFO components
    if ctx.components_list:
        info(f"Building components: {', '.join(ctx.components_list)}")
    else:
        info(f"Building components: ")
    # readme / index markdown
    readme_html=""
    readme_path=ctx.readme_path_cfg
    if os.path.exists(readme_path):
        # what if it's a directory/unreadable? original: if exists but read fails? We'll attempt read as asset - if fails, warning? Unknown. Use read; if directory, warn as not found? Probe later.
        try:
            with open(readme_path, "rb") as f:
                readme_bytes=f.read()
            readme_text=readme_bytes.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
            readme_html=render_markdown(readme_text, ctx)
        except OSError:
            warn_user(f"{readme_path} could not be found on disk!")
            readme_html=""
    else:
        warn_user(f"{readme_path} could not be found on disk!")
    ctx._readme_html=readme_html
    # Build component contents in memory (errors here leave only initial assets)
    changelog_content=None; rss_content=None
    changelog_page = bool(ctx.changelog_enabled and ctx.repository)
    if changelog_page:
        changelog_content=build_changelog_content(ctx)
        rss_content=build_rss(ctx)
    artifacts_content=None; artifacts_json_text=None
    artifacts_page = bool(ctx.artifacts_enabled and ctx.repository)
    if artifacts_page:
        artifacts_content=build_artifacts_content(ctx)
        model,_=artifacts_model(ctx)
        artifacts_json_text=json.dumps(model, separators=(",",":"), ensure_ascii=False)
    funding_content=None
    funding_page = bool(ctx.funding_enabled and ctx.repository)
    if funding_page:
        funding_content=build_funding_content(ctx)
    # mdbook building (may raise)
    mdbook_output_dir=None
    if ctx.mdbook_enabled:
        mdbook_output_dir=build_mdbook(ctx)  # returns intermediate output dir (book) to copy
    # warning about artifacts no releases (order: after INFO, before success, observed after INFO)
    if ctx.artifacts_enabled:
        if not ctx.releases or not ctx.releases.releases:
            warn_user("You seem to have release automation set up, but we didn't detect any releases. The install page and associated widget will be empty. To disable this, set `artifacts: false`")
    # ---- writing phase
    # logo file
    if ctx._logo_bytes is not None and ctx._logo_filename:
        _write_bytes_file(os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, ctx._logo_filename), ctx._logo_bytes)
    # index
    index_body=""
    if readme_html:
        index_body="\n          \n\n\n    " + readme_html + "\n\n\n"
    else:
        index_body="\n          \n\n\n\n"
    index_scripts="index_artifacts" if artifacts_page else "none"
    index_html=render_page(ctx, index_body, scripts_kind=index_scripts)
    _write_text_file(os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, "index.html"), index_html)
    # additional pages
    for (label, source_path, slug_path, md_html) in additional_pages_data:
        if md_html:
            body="\n          \n" + "  \n    " + md_html + "\n  \n\n"
        else:
            body="\n          \n" + "  \n\n  \n\n"
        page_html=render_page(ctx, body, scripts_kind="none")
        _write_text_file(os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, source_path), page_html)
    # changelog
    if changelog_page:
        body="\n          \n" + changelog_content + "\n"
        _write_text_file(os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, "changelog", "index.html"), render_page(ctx, body, scripts_kind="artifacts_page"))
        if rss_content is not None:
            _write_text_file(os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, "changelog.rss"), rss_content)
    # artifacts
    if artifacts_page:
        body="\n          \n" + artifacts_content + "\n"
        _write_text_file(os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, "artifacts", "index.html"), render_page(ctx, body, scripts_kind="artifacts_page"))
        _write_text_file(os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, "artifacts.json"), artifacts_json_text)
    # funding
    if funding_page:
        body="\n          \n" + funding_content + "\n"
        _write_text_file(os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, "funding", "index.html"), render_page(ctx, body, scripts_kind="none"))
    # mdbook copy to public/book
    if ctx.mdbook_enabled and mdbook_output_dir:
        dest_book=os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, "book")
        if os.path.isdir(dest_book):
            shutil.rmtree(dest_book)
        if os.path.isdir(mdbook_output_dir):
            shutil.copytree(mdbook_output_dir, dest_book)
    # custom favicon
    if ctx.favicon_path:
        fav_bytes=load_remote_or_local_asset(ctx.favicon_path, duplicate_cause=True)
        if ctx.favicon_path.startswith("http://") or ctx.favicon_path.startswith("https://"):
            fav_name=os.path.basename(urllib.parse.urlparse(ctx.favicon_path).path)
        else:
            fav_name=os.path.basename(ctx.favicon_path)
        if not fav_name:
            raise OrandaError(f"could not determine file name for asset at {ctx.favicon_path}", help_text="Make sure your path is relative to your oranda config or project manifest file.")
        _write_bytes_file(os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, fav_name), fav_bytes)
    # static
    copy_static(ctx)
    # artifacts.js
    _write_text_file(os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, "artifacts.js"), ARTIFACTS_JS)
    # additional css
    if ctx.additional_css:
        custom_parts=[]
        for css_path in ctx.additional_css:
            css_data=load_remote_or_local_asset(css_path, duplicate_cause=False)
            css_text=css_data.decode("utf-8", errors="replace") if isinstance(css_data,(bytes,bytearray)) else str(css_data)
            custom_parts.append(f"/* {css_path} */{css_text}")
        custom_css="".join(custom_parts)
        _write_text_file(os.path.join(ctx.dist_dir, "custom.css"), custom_css)
    success(f"Your site build is located in `{ctx.dist_dir}`.")
    return ctx

PY"}

def _exe_dir():
    argv0=sys.argv[0] if sys.argv else "executable"
    if "/" in argv0:
        p=os.path.realpath(argv0)
    else:

        p=os.path.realpath(found) if found else os.path.realpath(argv0)

We'll write prompts to sys.stderr if it's a tty else sys.stdout if it's a tty else stderr.

            # regular char

            if help_text:

            else:
                # no-help prompt is 1 line; move cursor?
                pass
            term_out.flush()
    finally:
        try: termios.tcsetattr(fd, termios.TCSADRAIN, old)
        except Exception: pass
    write_final(ans)
    return ans

def command_generate_ci(parsed):
    info("Generating a CI deploy workflow for your site...")
    output_path=parsed.get("output_path")
    if output_path is None:
        output_path=".github/workflows/web.yml"
    # file exists handling
    if os.path.exists(output_path):
        # Non-TTY quirk: unreadable/dir causes read error before prompt panic
        if not _is_tty():
            # try reading; if fails with non-NotFound, emit read error
            try:
                with open(output_path,"rb") as f: f.read()
            except OSError as e:
                raise OrandaError(f"failed to read asset from {output_path}", causes=[os_error_str(e)], help_text="Make sure your path is relative to your oranda config or project manifest file.")
        ans=_prompt_confirm(f"There's already a file at \"{output_path}\"! Do you want to override it?", default=False)
        if not ans:
            info("Ok, exiting...")
            return 0
        else:
            # after yes, attempt to read asset (observed); if fails, error
            try:
                with open(output_path,"rb") as f: f.read()
            except OSError as e:
                raise OrandaError(f"failed to read asset from {output_path}", causes=[os_error_str(e)], help_text="Make sure your path is relative to your oranda config or project manifest file.")
    linkcheck=_prompt_confirm("Do you want to include a tool for checking generated hyperlinks?", default=True, help_text="Read more about the link checker tool: https://github.com/untitaker/hyperlink")
    latest=_prompt_confirm("Do you want to always use the latest version of oranda?", default=False, help_text="Using the latest version means you don't have to rerun this command when oranda updates, but it may also break your site if you use a lot of configuration!")
    gitignore_yes=_prompt_confirm("Would you like to append the default destination directory (`public`) to your .gitignore file?", default=False)
    version_part="latest" if latest else VERSION_CSS
    # Template: base contains "releases/download/v0.6.1/..." vs "releases/latest/download/..."
    if latest:
        base=CI_TEMPLATE_BASE.replace("VERSION_PLACEHOLDER","latest")
        # our placeholder is in download/VERSION_PLACEHOLDER/
    else:
        base=CI_TEMPLATE_BASE.replace("VERSION_PLACEHOLDER", VERSION_CSS)
    content=base
    if linkcheck:
        content+=CI_TEMPLATE_LINKCHECK
    content+=CI_TEMPLATE_TAIL
    # write file (creates parent dirs)
    parent=os.path.dirname(output_path)
    if parent:
        try: os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
        except OSError as e:
            raise OrandaError(f"failed to write a new asset to {output_path}.", causes=[os_error_str(e)], help_text="Make sure you have the correct permissions to create a new file.")
    try:
        with open(output_path,"w",encoding="utf-8",newline="") as f: f.write(content)
    except OSError as e:
        raise OrandaError(f"failed to write a new asset to {output_path}.", causes=[os_error_str(e)], help_text="Make sure you have the correct permissions to create a new file.")
    if gitignore_yes:
        # append snippet
        try:
            with open(".gitignore","a",encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write("\n# Generated by `oranda generate ci`\npublic/")
        except OSError as e:
            # unknown original behaviour; ignore?
            pass
    success(f"Wrote CI file to \"{output_path}\"")
    return 0

def command_generate_ci(parsed):
    info("Generating a CI deploy workflow for your site...")
    output_path=parsed.get("output_path")
    if output_path is None:
        output_path=".github/workflows/web.yml"
    # file exists handling
    if os.path.exists(output_path):
        # Non-TTY quirk: unreadable/dir causes read error before prompt panic
        if not _is_tty():
            # try reading; if fails with non-NotFound, emit read error
            try:
                with open(output_path,"rb") as f: f.read()
            except OSError as e:
                raise OrandaError(f"failed to read asset from {output_path}", causes=[os_error_str(e)], help_text="Make sure your path is relative to your oranda config or project manifest file.")
        ans=_prompt_confirm(f"There's already a file at \"{output_path}\"! Do you want to override it?", default=False)
        if not ans:
            info("Ok, exiting...")
            return 0
        else:
            # after yes, attempt to read asset (observed); if fails, error
            try:
                with open(output_path,"rb") as f: f.read()
            except OSError as e:
                raise OrandaError(f"failed to read asset from {output_path}", causes=[os_error_str(e)], help_text="Make sure your path is relative to your oranda config or project manifest file.")
    linkcheck=_prompt_confirm("Do you want to include a tool for checking generated hyperlinks?", default=True, help_text="Read more about the link checker tool: https://github.com/untitaker/hyperlink")
    latest=_prompt_confirm("Do you want to always use the latest version of oranda?", default=False, help_text="Using the latest version means you don't have to rerun this command when oranda updates, but it may also break your site if you use a lot of configuration!")
    gitignore_yes=_prompt_confirm("Would you like to append the default destination directory (`public`) to your .gitignore file?", default=False)
    version_part="latest" if latest else VERSION_CSS
    # Template: base contains "releases/download/v0.6.1/..." vs "releases/latest/download/..."
    if latest:
        base=CI_TEMPLATE_BASE.replace("VERSION_PLACEHOLDER","latest")
        # our placeholder is in download/VERSION_PLACEHOLDER/
    else:
        base=CI_TEMPLATE_BASE.replace("VERSION_PLACEHOLDER", VERSION_CSS)
    content=base
    if linkcheck:
        content+=CI_TEMPLATE_LINKCHECK
    content+=CI_TEMPLATE_TAIL
    # write file (creates parent dirs)
    parent=os.path.dirname(output_path)
    if parent:
        try: os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
        except OSError as e:
            raise OrandaError(f"failed to write a new asset to {output_path}.", causes=[os_error_str(e)], help_text="Make sure you have the correct permissions to create a new file.")
    try:
        with open(output_path,"w",encoding="utf-8",newline="") as f: f.write(content)
    except OSError as e:
        raise OrandaError(f"failed to write a new asset to {output_path}.", causes=[os_error_str(e)], help_text="Make sure you have the correct permissions to create a new file.")

        try:

            # unknown original behaviour; ignore?
            pass

def _exe_dir():
    argv0=sys.argv[0] if sys.argv else "executable"
    if "/" in argv0:

def command_generate_ci(parsed):
    info("Generating a CI deploy workflow for your site...")
    output_path=parsed.get("output_path")
    if output_path is None:
        output_path=".github/workflows/web.yml"
    # file exists handling
    if os.path.exists(output_path):
        # Non-TTY quirk: unreadable/dir causes read error before prompt panic
        if not _is_tty():
            # try reading; if fails with non-NotFound, emit read error
            try:
                with open(output_path,"rb") as f: f.read()
            except OSError as e:
                raise OrandaError(f"failed to read asset from {output_path}", causes=[os_error_str(e)], help_text="Make sure your path is relative to your oranda config or project manifest file.")
        ans=_prompt_confirm(f"There's already a file at \"{output_path}\"! Do you want to override it?", default=False)
        if not ans:
            info("Ok, exiting...")
            return 0
        else:
            # after yes, attempt to read asset (observed); if fails, error
            try:
                with open(output_path,"rb") as f: f.read()
            except OSError as e:
                raise OrandaError(f"failed to read asset from {output_path}", causes=[os_error_str(e)], help_text="Make sure your path is relative to your oranda config or project manifest file.")
    linkcheck=_prompt_confirm("Do you want to include a tool for checking generated hyperlinks?", default=True, help_text="Read more about the link checker tool: https://github.com/untitaker/hyperlink")
    latest=_prompt_confirm("Do you want to always use the latest version of oranda?", default=False, help_text="Using the latest version means you don't have to rerun this command when oranda updates, but it may also break your site if you use a lot of configuration!")
    gitignore_yes=_prompt_confirm("Would you like to append the default destination directory (`public`) to your .gitignore file?", default=False)
    version_part="latest" if latest else VERSION_CSS
    # Template: base contains "releases/download/v0.6.1/..." vs "releases/latest/download/..."
    if latest:
        base=CI_TEMPLATE_BASE.replace("VERSION_PLACEHOLDER","latest")
        # our placeholder is in download/VERSION_PLACEHOLDER/
    else:
        base=CI_TEMPLATE_BASE.replace("VERSION_PLACEHOLDER", VERSION_CSS)
    content=base
    if linkcheck:
        content+=CI_TEMPLATE_LINKCHECK
    content+=CI_TEMPLATE_TAIL
    # write file (creates parent dirs)
    parent=os.path.dirname(output_path)
    if parent:
        try: os.makedirs(parent, exist_ok=True)
        except OSError as e:
            raise OrandaError(f"failed to write a new asset to {output_path}.", causes=[os_error_str(e)], help_text="Make sure you have the correct permissions to create a new file.")
    try:
        with open(output_path,"w",encoding="utf-8",newline="") as f: f.write(content)
    except OSError as e:
        raise OrandaError(f"failed to write a new asset to {output_path}.", causes=[os_error_str(e)], help_text="Make sure you have the correct permissions to create a new file.")
    if gitignore_yes:
        # append snippet
        try:
            with open(".gitignore","a",encoding="utf-8") as f: f.write("\n# Generated by `oranda generate ci`\npublic/")
        except OSError as e:
            # unknown original behaviour; ignore?
            pass
    success(f"Wrote CI file to \"{output_path}\"")
    return 0

#!/bin/sh
set -e
cd "$(dirname "$0")"
# Bundle the Python implementation into a single executable script.
python3 - << 'PY'
import pathlib
main = pathlib.Path("main.py").read_text()
assets = pathlib.Path("assets_data.py").read_text()
#Inline assets: replace the assets import block with the actual data definitions

bundle = main.replace(
    "try:\n    from assets_data import SCHEMA_JSON, ARTIFACTS_JS, FAVICON_B64, MD_BOOK_ASSETS\nexcept Exception:  # when bundled into a single file by compile.sh, assets are inlined below\n    SCHEMA_JSON = \"{}\"\n    ARTIFACTS_JS = \"\"\n    FAVICON_B64 = \"\"\n    MD_BOOK_ASSETS = {}",
    assets
)
if "SCHEMA_JSON = " not in bundle:
    raise SystemExit("failed to inline assets")
pathlib.Path("executable").write_text(bundle)
PY

def parse_json_with_serde(text, spec, filename_display):
    """Parse and validate, raising OrandaError('failed to parse JSON') on failure."""
    try:
        parser = JsonParser(text)
        try:
            node = parser.parse()
        except SerdeJsonError as syntax_e:
            semantic = _try_partial_semantic(text, spec, syntax_e)
            if semantic is not None:
                _raise_serde_as_oranda(text, semantic, filename_display)
            raise
        value = validate_node(node, spec, text) if not isinstance(spec, StructSpec) else validate_struct(node, spec, text)
        return value
    except SerdeJsonError as e:
        if e.label_offset is None:
            # empty source
            msg = f"{e.msg} at line 1 column 0"
            err = OrandaError("failed to parse JSON", causes=[msg], filename="", label_offset=None, source_text=text)
            # filename is empty string in json mode, no snippet
            err._empty_source = True
            raise err
        line, col = serde_line_col(text, e.label_offset)
        msg = f"{e.msg} at line {line} column {col}"
        # byte offset
        byte_offset = len(text[:e.label_offset].encode("utf-8")) if isinstance(text, str) else e.label_offset
        err = OrandaError("failed to parse JSON", causes=[msg], filename=filename_display, label_offset=e.label_offset, source_text=text)
        err._byte_offset = byte_offset
        raise err
